connectors.evidence_source: metadata docs_url; Discord's provider-published llms index and its complete current Markdown reference pages
connectors.counting_note: Counted every current provider-documented HTTP <Route> action block in Discord's llms-indexed reference: 204 actions across 22 HTTP-resource pages, plus 16 application-command, eight interaction-response, two Gateway REST, and two OAuth2 current-information actions. Method split is 96 GET, 40 POST, 24 PUT, 33 PATCH, and 39 DELETE. GET actions are reads; every non-GET action creates, responds, invokes, modifies, links, deletes, or otherwise changes provider state, so is a write. Separately headed current action blocks sharing a route were retained (thread variants, lobby link/unlink, DM versus group DM, and interaction followup versus generic webhook actions). Deprecated/current endpoint pairs appearing only as changelog examples were excluded. Inbound Gateway and webhook event types are excluded; the two documented Gateway REST discovery endpoints are retained.

connectors.evidence_source: metadata docs_url; Fastly's provider-published API Reference linking this downloadable Postman collection, plus direct parse of its request inventory
connectors.counting_note: Parsed Fastly's provider-linked downloadable Postman collection. Its 740 request items normalize to 732 unique method/path operations; eight exact duplicate method/path pairs were collapsed. Sixteen direct credential-support actions are excluded consistently with r1: 13 automation/user-token actions, password update/reset, and sudo re-authentication. Of the 716 remaining data operations, 336 GET actions are reads, as are three explicit stateless/validation POSTs (one WAF request simulation and two VCL lint validations). The other 119 POST, 86 PUT, 50 PATCH, and 122 DELETE operations create, alter, publish, purge, notify, or remove provider state and are writes. The POST alert test sends a notification and is therefore a write. No inbound webhook-delivery schema is included in this collection; configuration resources are retained.
